newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU sees cut-throat competition at wheat tender.
newsitem.headline: EU sees cut-throat competition at wheat tender.

text.p: The European Commission expects cut-throat competition among frantic exporters bidding for wheat export licences at this week's grain tender, EU grain sources said on Tuesday.

Traders scrambling to meet a surge in wheat offtake while facing the threat of a slowdown in EU exports may end up substantially cutting their bids for wheat export rebates in the last grain tender for 1996, they predicted.
"We are expecting (rebate bids of) seven to eight Ecus per tonne this week," one source said.
Last week the European Union granted 477,700 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a rebate of 17.47 Ecus per tonne, valuing French wheat at around $154 per tonne, fob.
It is crucial for exporters to secure export licences this week because the Commission will be closed for business between Christmas and the New Year.

Exporters are in an especially tight spot because EU agriculture director Guy Legras has warned the EU may slow its wheat exports after authorising more than one million tonnes of wheat in the previous two weeks.
All these elements combined with firmer world wheat prices may lead exporters to massively bid for wheat export licences this week at substantially low rebates, sources said.
"This will be a battle field. There will be bloodshed. They (traders) are totally panicky," one source said.
What makes the situation especially tricky is that exporters have a larger than expected short position, which the source estimated at some 500,000 tonnes.

This is mostly because exporters have been under-reporting recent business deals to eastern Europe and north Africa while complaining they were missing export opportunities on world markets to cheaper supplies from Argentina and Australia, one source said.
Demand for European Union wheat may also get a boost from poor weather hitting Argentine and U.S. crops, the source said.
"People have been spinning a lot of tales," he said.
Over the last two weeks operators have been trying to secure export licences to help cover deals to North Africa and eastern Europe.
But two trade houses have managed to get hold of most of the licences available, bringing the EU to announce it may "turn the screw" on exports.

Last Thursday European Union traders bid to export 1.7 million tonnes of wheat through the weekly grain tender channel and on Friday Legras linked the massive bids to a few "wise guys" trying to play games.
Grain industry sources said Legras' export warning was also aimed at keeping wheat prices in check within the EU. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
